lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Susan, it's Ana. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How have you been feeling since we last talked?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've had more energy, I noticed that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it! 3 out of 3 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're really honest with yourself, and that helps.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, sometimes. I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Cooking a big pot on Sunday can cover two or three dinners.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd do it if the day had a few more hours.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the soda swap. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I can cook on Sunday and have it for a few days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the soda swap going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Cooking a big pot on Sunday can cover two or three dinners.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've been really tired.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Let's say I cook at home 3 nights.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 7.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 7 and not a 4?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If being so tired gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll do it right when I wake up, before anything else.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Susan, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Ana. Bye!

tags.note: Offers agenda and invites her input
States ability to manage three days
Fatigue and daughter not available as barrier
Pushes toward five days before she is ready
Reason: wants it for her mental health
Reflects a conditional that she did not state
Asserts the deeper meaning of the goal for her
Verbatim repeat of line 19 after she was not receptive
Wants to keep up with grandchildren
Recognizes her knowledge of her schedule
Past success as evidence of ability

flags.reason: Asked whether 5 days is realistic right after she reported exhaustion, pushing a goal she had not chosen.
Asserted what the goal means ('getting your life back') rather than asking what matters to her.
Re-offered the same suggestion (lines 40-42) after she had not engaged, instead of exploring her barriers.
Fatigue ('I don't have it in me') and later 'for my head' were not explored for low mood or energy changes.

score.summary: Ana drew out strong change talk, including Susan's commitment to cook three nights and her confidence rating of 7. However, she repeated the same advice verbatim, pushed a five-day goal, and did not explore Susan's fatigue or emotional cues.
strengths: Line 10 and 11: affirmed Susan's honesty and reflected her ambivalence as fair.
Line 48: recognized Susan's knowledge of her own schedule.
Line 54 and 56: asked why her confidence was 7 and planned for the backup if fatigue returns.
coaching_tips: Line 42: repeating the line 19 suggestion verbatim after Susan did not engage; instead ask what has made the plan hard.
Line 15: avoid pressing the 5-day goal when she has just described exhaustion; ask what range feels right.
Line 32: replace the 'getting your life back' framing with an open question about what matters most to her.
Line 14: explore the fatigue and mood cues ('for my head') with an open question before moving to a plan.
Line 51: vary affirmations; the repeat of line 48 sounds scripted. Summarize the plan before closing.
